title: The closure of a generated subsystem is the subsystem itself
source_title: The elementary theory of free Steiner triple systems

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of the labelled lemma, retained line for line

standard_prerequisites.name: Generated subsystem
standard_prerequisites.statement: The subsystem generated by A is the union of the finite stages obtained by closing under products of two elements already present.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the subsystem whose closure is computed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Closure operator
standard_prerequisites.statement: The closure under an ordering is a finitary closure operator and distributes over binary unions.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the operator applied to the stages.

core_obligations: Write the generated subsystem as the union of its finite stages and observe that it suffices to prove by induction on the stage that the closure of each finite union of stages equals that union (source line 362).
Check the initial stage, where the equality is the hypothesis that A equals its closure (source line 362).

For the induction step, use that a new element of the next stage is a product of two elements of the current union and that the closure is closed under forming such products, so it is already in the closure of the current union (source line 362).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to the finite stages and set up the induction.
Propagate the equality along the stages using closure under products.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 358-360: for an HF-ordering of M, a subset A and the assumption that A equals its closure, the closure of the subsystem generated by A is that subsystem. The proof (source lines 361-363) replaces the generated subsystem by its presentation as a union of finite stages, reduces the claim to an induction on the stage, and the whole content of the induction step is the observation that a new element is a product of two elements of the previous union, so that the closure of that union already contains it because the closure is closed under forming blocks from elements already present. The statement records only the equality.
